Definition: the constellation of the Great Bear (perhaps from its migration through the heavens)
BiblicalUsage: Ayish is the Great Bear, the constellation Job names among the wonders God made — Arcturus, Orion and the Pleiades — and which God himself names when he answers Job out of the whirlwind. A star-picture in the northern sky, set there by the same hand that set the Pleiades.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the stars are God's handiwork, not man's fortune-telling, and the Great Bear still turns in its course because he holds it there.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
